leading_positions.synthesis: Three members put targeted protein degradation first as a designable chemical principle (induced proximity, removal rather than inhibition). All three name Crews and Deshaies. They differ on the third laureate: Ciulli (Aili, Aqvist, for structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work) versus Handa (Chabes, for identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target). Aili and Aqvist treat PROTACs and cereblon-based glues as separate strands and would keep a PROTAC-centred citation; Chabes argues the shared E3-redirection mechanism lets one citation cover both. All three concede that no PROTAC is approved and that Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim are left out.

Two members put Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling first, with Buchwald and Hartwig as a two-person prize and the cleanest attribution and maturity on the shortlist. They argue that C-N coupling needed its own mechanistic and ligand solution (amine binding, C-N reductive elimination) and so is distinct from the 2010 C-C prize. They differ on how to treat Kosugi and Migita: Somfai would acknowledge them in the background text or wording, Zou would use the words general and catalytic in the citation. Several other members rank B057 as an alternative, but only these two prefer it in their configuration.

Two members prefer biomolecular phase separation as a physical-chemical principle of cellular organisation, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen and a citation worded identically in both files. Both want the citation held to the organising principle and not to claimed functions of particular condensates, and both state that in-cell functional relevance is still debated. They differ on emphasis: Sparr stresses chemical measurables and prefers Rosen over Pappu for the third place; Linke asks whether Pappu and Mittag contributed quantitative work that Rosen's contribution does not cover. Linke is the chair and his position is reported on the same basis as the others.

One member prefers energy-landscape theory of protein folding (Wolynes, Onuchic, Fersht) as a mature, mechanism-level physical principle and as complementary to, not redundant with, the 2024 prize. Sparr ranks it among her alternatives and Aili calls it a good fallback. Credit is shared with Bryngelson and Dill, and the theory-versus-experiment pairing with Fersht is questioned by the chair.

areas_of_agreement: No single ballot is preferred by a majority of five. The preferred configurations split three (B068), two (B057), two (B022) and one (B027), and every member stated a single-ballot preference.
Members on several sides (Aqvist, Aili, Brzezinski, Zou, Somfai, Sparr, Linke) accept that induced proximity is a genuine new principle, and Brzezinski and Linke keep B068 among their alternatives.
Members agree that B057 is the cleanest on maturity and attribution, and that the real question is conceptual novelty relative to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Members agree that B022 and B068 each have open questions that bear on citation wording: in-cell relevance for condensates and the PROTAC versus glue split for degraders.
All eight members state that no specific conflict is apparent.
scientific_disputes: Whether C-N coupling is a distinct mechanistic advance (Somfai, Zou: amine binding and difficult C-N reductive elimination solved by ligand design) or a ligand-driven extension of a recognised reaction class (Aqvist, Chabes, Aili, Sparr, Linke raise this).

Whether in-vitro phase separation reflects liquid-liquid phase separation in living cells and whether it is chemistry. Linke and Sparr treat the principle as well supported, and Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Somfai, Chabes and Zou doubt that functional claims are settled.
Whether PROTAC design and cereblon-mediated glue degradation are one scientific achievement or two (Chabes: one mechanism; Aili, Aqvist, Somfai, Zou, Sparr, Linke: separate or unresolved).

What the funnel picture predicted beyond what folding kinetics already showed, and how much weight the 2024 prize carries against B027 (Brzezinski: complementary; Sparr, Linke: overlap or limited novelty).
attribution_disputes: B068 third laureate: Ciulli (Aili, Aqvist) versus Handa (Chabes), with Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim excluded and acknowledged as contestable by the supporters.

B022: whether Rosen or Pappu and Mittag belongs in the third place, and how credit divides between the founding observation of liquid P granules (Hyman, Brangwynne) and the multivalent molecular grammar.
B057: Kosugi and Migita precedent in tin-amide amination, and whether it should be acknowledged in the citation or only in the background.
B027: Bryngelson and Dill priority claims, and whether Wolynes and Onuchic (theory) and Fersht (experiment) form one discovery.

Apparently similar proposals differ in laureates and citation: B068 appears as a Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli citation about heterobifunctional PROTACs (Aqvist, Aili) and as a Crews, Deshaies, Handa citation covering PROTACs and glue mechanism (Chabes). B022 appears with identical laureates and nearly identical citations from Linke and Sparr.
maturity_disputes: No PROTAC or degrader is approved. Aili and Aqvist treat reproducibility and the clinical pipeline as sufficient, while Chabes, Somfai, Brzezinski and Zou see timing risk or ask for the expert reports to separate chemistry from drug-development momentum.
In-cell relevance of condensates is unsettled, and the supporters (Linke, Sparr) and sceptics disagree whether it is a reason to wait or only to word the citation carefully.
B057 is fully mature (four decades), and its critics ask only about novelty, not maturity.
B027 is mature as theory, but Sparr says it has been less directly tested than the condensate work.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Sparr discloses that she directs a membrane and lipid research centre overlapping in topic with B054 (ionizable lipid nanoparticles, an alternative for her) and, more loosely, B022. She states that no recusal appears necessary.
Aili notes loose thematic proximity of his biosensor and bioengineering work to nanoparticle and delivery topics such as B054, and no recusal is indicated.

Linke, Somfai and Sparr share a Lund affiliation, and Brzezinski is a Stockholm University colleague of Zou. All members say these are colleague relationships and not candidate connections, and no recusal is claimed.
questions_for_round2: B068: is the discovery the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept or the cereblon glue mechanism, and if the prize is for PROTACs, which of Ciulli or Handa should hold the third place? Can one citation honestly cover both strands?
B068: is the absence of an approved degrader a reason to wait, or only a reason to word the citation around the mechanism of degradation and not the clinical pipeline?

B057: what exactly is conceptually new relative to the 2010 prize, and does the committee consider the C-N ligand and mechanism problem a separate discovery or a sequel? How should Kosugi and Migita be acknowledged?

B022: is the principle of liquid-like demixing in cells established independently of claimed condensate functions, and is it chemistry? Should the third laureate be Rosen or Pappu, and does Mittag's work change that?
B027: what did the funnel picture predict that folding kinetics did not already show, and does the 2024 prize reduce the case for it? Is the citation honouring theory, experiment or both?

Does any member see a two-part configuration (for example a B057 part together with a single-laureate part) as drawing more support than the four single-ballot positions now on the table, and which members could move to a shared first choice?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows four distinct single-ballot preferences and no majority, with three members on B068, two each on B057 and B022, and one on B027. Cross-support exists but is not yet a preferred configuration: B057, B068 and B022 each appear as alternatives in several files. The decisive open items are the credit cut for B068, the novelty argument for B057 and the in-cell evidence for B022. These can be addressed by round-2 answers and should not be read as a ruling.
